concerns.text: The Linear Mixed‑Effects Model (FR‑004) includes species as a random intercept, yet the cross‑validation scheme (FR‑006) splits data strictly by species. When a species is held out, its random‑effect term cannot be estimated from the training data, making out‑of‑sample predictions for that species unreliable and rendering the reported out‑of‑sample adjusted R² (SC‑002) potentially invalid.

FR‑001 requires a minimum of 20 observations per species for inclusion, while the a priori power analysis (FR‑024) targets ≥30 observations per species to achieve 80 % power. Species with 20–29 observations will be retained but will not meet the power requirement, creating a mismatch that can leave the study under‑powered for many species and jeopardize the validity of SC‑009.

Success criterion SC‑002 defines achievement as the LMM adjusted R² being within 5 percentage points of the random‑forest R². Both metrics are derived from the same dataset and thus are not independent ground‑truth references for the hypothesised nutrient‑architecture relationship; using one model’s performance as a benchmark for the other creates a circular validation of the effect rather than an independent test of the hypothesis.
